row, a stronger replacement, or a helper used by an existing row.
2. Inspect the current types before designing another abstraction. For finite packets, reuse range sub-
types and actual Hom blocks. For topology, use continuous linear maps and state completeness
where it is needed.
3. Separate supplied data from proved consequences. A new canonical-form constructor should have
its own existence theorem, not only a theorem taking a canonical-form certificate as an argument.
4. Prove or import the bridge from the new representation to the manuscript’s object. A result about a
bespoke rank predicate needs a theorem relating it to canonical seed rank before it can replace the
existing formula.
5. Compile the changed modules in the pinned environment, update the normative map deliberately,
and update the audit inventory to exactly the desired mapped surface.
6. Run the explicit audit and the full verifier with a new output directory. Preserve prior records and
record new hashes rather than overwriting the date of the old evidence.
7. Review the new source-to-prose correspondence. Kernel acceptance proves the typed theorem. The
review establishes that this is the intended theorem and that its public summary retains the hypothe-
ses.

A guide to the actual formal development. 20 scoped manuscript results. 225 theorem targets. 23
proof modules. The eight tutorial chapters explain the route from literal samples to Hilbert oper-
ators, finite filters, packet synthesis, adaptive trees, and projective actions. The complete ledgers
then give exact declarations and manuscript locators.
The full traditional edition also contains 63 broader prose proof records. Their separate inventory
is a reading aid and adds no formal coverage. The two edge recovery conjectures remain open.
This edition preserves 52 exact Lean excerpts and reconciles source bytes, declaration locations,
dependency pins, and the saved axiom audit. Kernel execution evidence comes from the recorded

edits.old_text_exact:
This chapter develops the transfer-semigroup realization of the projector-resolved seed calculus.
A seed is propagated by a one-parameter semigroup, a Markov kernel, a normalized Bayesian trans-
fer, a fractional spectral power, a Green operator, or a potential-weighted Feynman–Kac operator.
Exact packet projectors resolve every transfer into input-output blocks, and the semigroup law be-
comes block convolution over intermediate packets. Coarse and fine generators are compared by a
refinement defect. A Duhamel identity proves that this generator-level defect is exactly the source
of the corresponding semigroup defect and gives a quantitative stability bound. In the stochastic
realization, point-mass seeds generate random walks and continuous-time Markov evolution. Ex-
act lumpability is the vanishing of the same refinement defect. Conditional expectation is treated
as a weighted orthogonal packet projector, with nested partitions producing martingale-difference
packets. Bayesian conditioning is a normalized nonlinear operator. Its independent-data composi-
tion law, packet-evidence decomposition, stability bound, conjugate updates, and continuous likeli-
hood flow are proved explicitly. The Bayesian refinement conjecture is resolved in finite dimensions:
for strictly positive likelihoods and at least two coarse packets, exact commutation for every prior
is equivalent to blockwise-constant likelihoods up to global scale, and every failure factors through
an explicit information-loss packet. Fractional powers are constructed packetwise through the spec-
tral projectors of a positive operator, and the square-root semigroup is recovered by subordination.
The fractional-naturality conjecture is also resolved for bounded nonnegative self-adjoint refinement
systems: the fractional intertwining defect has an exact resolvent integral, a gap-free Hölder cer-
tificate, a sharper common-gap estimate, and a Duhamel semigroup bound. Green kernels, finite-
difference Poisson problems, and second-order low-mode convergence provide the PDE realization.
A finite-state Feynman–Kac formula is proved by path enumeration. Exact Schur–Feshbach elim-
ination shows that discarded latent packets return as a frequency-dependent self-energy and, in
time coordinates, as a memory kernel. Survival and hazard functions are generated by transient
semigroups. Nineteen code-generated figures, machine-readable results, the original thirty-seven
automated tests, and seventeen added boundary-case checks accompany this reviewed edition. The
inherited September 6 release records five checked Lean blocks covering all 33 scoped theorem-like
results in Appendix A. Finite-dimensional theorems, classical infinite-dimensional extensions, nu-
merical certificates, and open continuum claims are kept separate.

Conditional expectation is treated as a weighted orthogonal packet projector, with nested partitions producing martingale-difference packets. Bayesian conditioning is a normalized nonlinear operator. Its independent-data composition law, packet-evidence decomposition, stability bound, conjugate updates, and continuous likelihood flow are proved explicitly. The Bayesian refinement conjecture is resolved in finite dimensions: for strictly positive likelihoods and at least two coarse packets, exact commutation for every prior is equivalent to blockwise-constant likelihoods up to global scale, and every failure factors through an explicit information-loss packet. declarations written for Paper XII, including supporting lemmas and interface results. A further 81

not itself rebuilt. Exact compiler results, source hashes, and the verification scope are recorded with the
archive.
The preserved release records complete mapped Lean statements for all 49 internal numbered
claims of its revised manuscript. The present traditional edition retains those proof bodies, exposes
the hypotheses on the local map and coefficient target in proposition 3.3, makes the r > n convention
explicit in the proof of theorem 6.4, states all the pointwise comparison inputs in definition 12.1, and
declares a finite ramification set and coherent geometric Frobenius normalization. These editorial
clarifications are recorded separately from the inherited eight amendments. They are not counted as
newly compiled Lean certificates. No new statement amendment was needed for the completion and
tensor results. The eight inherited amendments remain explicitly separate from the original wording,

hypotheses, not every prose claim, novelty assertion, or external arithmetic result.
The completion block proves theorem 3.1 and proposition 3.3 using actual algebraic tensor products,
actual Hausdorff completions, and the actual closed generated ideals. Both inverse laws, continuity
in both directions, and the canonical factor maps are checked. An independent comparison with the
algebraic inverse limit completion identifies the topology and local ring structure. The global theorem
retains continuous local algebra points and their naturality, rather than only an unstructured point
existence statement. The empty family retains the scalar adic topology. The zero condition and unit
ideal boundaries are checked separately.
The preceding Fitting block proves theorems 6.3, 6.4 and 7.1 and proposition 6.5. Its intrinsic Fitting
ideals are independent of the chosen finite presentation, including the number of generators and
relations. Arbitrary base change, all higher fiber dimension strata, and the complete support and Fitting
transport statement are checked. The Noetherian and finite module hypotheses of the manuscript
provide the finite presentation needed by the general construction.

transfer and augmentation. Coinvariant recovery uses the quotient by all balancing relations, with its
universal property proved. In the commutative case, this construction is identified with the ordinary
tensor product. The augmentation relations generate exactly the augmentation ideal acting on the
module. Applying augmentation to the coordinates of a supplied free basis gives a coefficient basis

bined verification entry point is:
python3 VERIFY_PAPER.py

consistency checks. Lean, Lake, the pinned dependencies, the Python requirements, and a TeX installa-
tion must be available for the corresponding full checks. Missing prerequisites or failed checks return
failure. Static checks alone never report kernel verification. The individual numerical generation com-
mand is

python3 run_all.py

The TeX source resolves the eighteen vector figures from the manuscript’s figure directory. The checked
build uses repeated pdfLaTeX passes, then text, cross-reference, and page-render inspection. Different
pdfTeX versions can produce different binary PDF hashes even when the rendered document is un-
changed.
In the September 2026 release environment, a disclosed runtime adapter was needed for Lean
executable-path discovery: it redirects a read of the current process’s numeric /proc executable link
to /proc/self/exe. It does not modify the Lean binary, elaborator, kernel, axioms, or proof terms. The
adapter source and invocation are retained with the verification evidence. Ordinary installations can
run the pinned toolchain directly.

pleted source/object hash and dependency closure, reused only those 422 successful objects from this session,

pendent completed in 1,066.8 and 827.6 seconds, respectively, completing all 423 selected modules. The terminal
then emitted substantive elaboration errors, including a heartbeat-limit diagnostic. After inspection of its log,
that process known to have failed was deliberately terminated. This second run also remains PARTIAL_OR_FAIL. It
was stopped in response to those diagnostics.

the revised failed terminal. Its terminal process was then killed at the environment’s 8 GiB memory limit. The
recorded out-of-memory counters increased. This third replay also remains failed. An unchanged-source contin-
uation with synchronous elaboration, Elab.async=false, also reached the memory limit. That fourth full replay
remains failed. Bounded diagnostics isolated an expensive conversion in the lower-inclusion witness. The fi-
nal continuation authenticated the successful closure and compiled separately reviewed local proof repairs. No

sources were not rebuilt.
